methodNote: Every other file in this directory was produced by `pnpm indexed:first-contact`, which makes four
real requests per source and records the wire response. THIS FILE WAS NOT. No request was made to
news.google.com by this project, at any time, and none should be.
The reason is the finding itself. Act one of the onboarding procedure exists to gather what the
person taking the first-contact approval needs in order to take it. Here the publisher's own
published terms answer the question before the endpoint is reached, and they answer it with a
prohibition on automated access. Loading the feed to 'check' would be performing the exact act the
terms forbid, and would do so in order to decide whether the terms forbid it. So the evidence stops
at the terms, deliberately, and this file records no httpStatus, no wireBytes and no body hash for
the endpoint, because none was observed.
A future reader must not treat the absence of those fields as an incomplete evidence run to be

finding: Independently of the licence question, the feed cannot meet this service's provenance
requirement. Since late 2024 a Google News RSS <item><link> is not the publisher's article URL.
It is a Google-hosted redirect of the form https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi<token>?oc=5.
There are exactly two ways to recover the publisher's article URL from that token, and this
1. Follow the redirect — another automated request to news.google.com, which is the prohibited act.
2. Decode the token locally — base64 yields a protobuf carrying Google's own internal article
identifier rather than a URL, and resolving it requires a signature that cannot be computed
offline. Reverse-engineering it is scraping Google by another name.
The feed's <source url="..."> element does carry the publisher's DOMAIN (e.g. reuters.com), but a
domain is not an article. FR-09 provenance requires the exact document a finding came from, and a
finding that names a domain and cannot name the document is a finding a reviewer cannot check.

note: Deliberately not fetched. robots.txt governs crawling; it cannot grant what the Terms of Use
withhold, so reading it could not change the outcome. Recording it as NOT_READ rather than
NOT_ESTABLISHED keeps the distinction honest: nobody looked, and nobody needed to.

summary: Google News RSS has no defensible commercial access basis for this service. The Google News Terms
of Use restrict the service to personal, non-commercial display, and separately prohibit using any
robot or automated process to monitor or copy content. This is a commercial B2B screening product.
The terms are dated 2006 and Google publishes no documentation for the /rss/search endpoint at all.
That combination is not a loophole — an undocumented endpoint carries no separate grant, so the
general terms are the only terms there are, and they say no.

legitimateAlternative.product: Google Programmable Search Engine / Custom Search JSON API
why: Documented, contractually licensed, and sold for commercial use — the three things the RSS feed
lacks. It returns publisher URLs directly, so the provenance defect above does not arise.
It is paid beyond a free daily allowance, which makes it a commercial decision rather than an
engineering one, and it is therefore out of scope for a project whose stated constraint is free
and open-source sources only. Recorded here so the next reader does not re-derive it.
